title: Intellectual Property: Trade Secrets vs. Patents

parts.visual:
A company's most valuable asset is often its ideas. But how do you protect an idea?

The Executive Choice:
1. The Patent: You register the invention with the government. You get a 20-year legal monopoly to sell it. The catch: You must publish the exact blueprints publicly for anyone to read.
2. The Trade Secret: You never tell the government. You lock the recipe in a vault. The catch: If someone reverse-engineers it legally, you have zero protection.
parts.audio: To protect an invention, executives must choose between a Patent and a Trade Secret. A patent gives you a 20-year monopoly, but you must publish your blueprints to the world.

questions.question: The recipe for Coca-Cola has never been patented. It is protected as a 'Trade Secret'. Why did the executives make this choice?
options: Because a patent expires after 20 years, allowing anyone to legally copy it. A trade secret lasts forever, as long as you can keep it hidden.
Because they forgot to file the paperwork.
questions.correct_answer: Because a patent expires after 20 years, allowing anyone to legally copy it. A trade secret lasts forever, as long as you can keep it hidden.
questions.explanation: If Coca-Cola had patented their recipe in 1886, the recipe would have become public knowledge, and legally free to copy, in 1906.

questions.question: Listen to the Chief Technology Officer. Why is he demanding a patent?
questions.tts_text: If we release this new hardware, our competitors will buy it, take it apart, and reverse-engineer how we built it in under a month.
options: Because it is easy to keep a secret.
Because if a product is easily reverse-engineered, a Trade Secret is useless. You must rely on the legal protection of a Patent.
questions.correct_answer: Because if a product is easily reverse-engineered, a Trade Secret is useless. You must rely on the legal protection of a Patent.
questions.explanation: You cannot keep a physical machine a secret once you sell it to the public. You must patent the mechanics.

questions.question: What is the fatal flaw of relying on a Trade Secret?
options: If another company independently discovers the exact same formula through their own research, they can legally use it, and you cannot stop them.
questions.correct_answer: If another company independently discovers the exact same formula through their own research, they can legally use it, and you cannot stop them.
questions.explanation: Trade secrets only protect you against espionage and theft. They do not protect you against independent genius.

questions.question: What does it mean when a patent enters the 'Public Domain'?
options: The 20-year legal monopoly has expired. The invention is now free for any company in the world to manufacture and sell without paying royalties.
questions.correct_answer: The 20-year legal monopoly has expired. The invention is now free for any company in the world to manufacture and sell without paying royalties.
questions.explanation: This is the core bargain of the patent system: Short-term monopoly in exchange for long-term human progress.
